text:
sam: Noticed steady RSS growth on long-chat sessions even after KV eviction kicks in. Heap snapshots look like a lot of tiny free holes + many small live blobs that don't get reused. Repro in staging attached below. :thinking:

alex: Ugh i've seen that — sounds like micro-frag from our allocator + KV shard churn. Any recent changes to block size distribution or LRU policy?

maria: We bumped `min_block = 64` -> `128` for some throughput wins last month, could be related. Also we changed the LRU eviction to be per-shard instead of global.

sam: right — repro runs show a rising count of free fragments in the 64-256 byte range. When sequence length is large and many prefixes are cached+evicted, reuse rate drops. Here's a quick pprof snippet from the run: 

```
heap: 2.1G total
  820MB kv_cache_entries (many ~160B)
  540MB free_fragments (64-256B bins)
  240MB transient_allocs
  500MB other
```

sam: Also saw the allocator favoring different block sizes per shard; some shards have >70% fragmentation.

priya: Could be LRU signature collisions — if we hash keys into a small signature space for quick LRU buckets, eviction can evict items that would have been coalesced, leaving interleaved holes. Did you check signature bucket occupancy?

sam: Good call. I ran a quick sampler: many buckets have 1-3 entries but a long tail with 0, and collision rate ~8% for 1024 buckets.

zach: 8% collision seems plausible to hurt micro-coalescing. Maybe increase signature bits or use per-shard dynamic bucket counts. But that increases metadata.

alex: Another angle: compaction. We currently only do full compaction at shutdown and opportunistic adjacent-coalesce on free list mutation. What about a background compactor that targets small-frag bins and uses an age-weighted score?

maria: Sketch: compute a compaction_score for a region = (free_frag_count_in_range * avg_age_of_free) / (live_entry_density + 1). Run compaction if score > threshold. Could we throttle to avoid CPU blow?

sam: Love the age-weighting idea. I prototyped a lightweight compaction that scans hot shards every 30s and attempts to merge holes up to 1KB budget. Results: peak RSS reduced ~12% on the staging run, but CPU + tail latency increased for a short burst during compaction.

priya: Do you have the proto commands? Want to run on a few failsafe hosts.

sam: Yep: 

```bash
# run compactor proto with 1KB budget per shard, adaptive throttle
./kv_compactor --budget=1024 --scan-interval=30s --throttle=adaptive --sig-buckets=2048
```

sam: Also added a mitigation: when allocating, prefer smallest-fitting free fragment within the same signature bucket first — increases locality of reuse.

zach: That alloc preference might help a lot; keeps related KVs colocated so future reuses are contiguous. Any metrics?

sam: Quick numbers from the prototype: reuse hit rate on small bins up from 21% -> 44%, free_frag_count down 30%, tail p99 latency bump +0.9ms during compaction windows.

alex: Sounds promising. Two follow-ups: (1) run A/B in staging with compactor enabled on 10% of nodes for a day, collect p99+cpu; (2) evaluate increasing signature space from 1024 -> 4096 vs metadata cost.

maria: I'll add a config flag toggle for compactor and sig-buckets to remote config. Also document the per-shard memory metadata delta.

dev-bot: Deployment flag `kv_compactor_enabled` created in experiment namespace `kv-frag-compactor-v1` by maria. :white_check_mark:

infra-ops-bot: Scheduled canary: 10% of staging nodes at 03:15 UTC tomorrow. Monitoring: kv.rss, kv.free_frag_count, kv.reuse_rate, host.cpu. Alerts if p99 latency increases >5% or CPU > +20%.

priya: I'll run the A/B harness and add a microbenchmark that stresses prefix churn (long contexts + heavy rerank).

sam: Action items I have: push compactor binary with adaptive throttle, add alloc pref change, run canary, gather detailed bucket occupancy histograms.

azach: (typo) zach: I'll help with the histograms and a small simulation to try variable block size policies — can share a script.

sam: Great — let's keep the compactor opt-in until we've got solid telemetry. Thanks all :raised_hands: 

alex: SGTM. If compaction works we should add a low-cost offline compaction during quiet periods on Dedicated nodes as well.

maria: noted, filing a follow-up RFC after we have 24h canary data.

sam: End of thread — will post results tomorrow. :eyes:
